title: arenaria modesta subsp. algarbiensis
intro: Arenaria modesta subsp. algarbiensis, commonly known as the Algarve sandwort, is a plant species within the carnation family (Caryophyllaceae) that is native to the Iberian Peninsula. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including inflammation and respiratory problems, due to its potential health benefits. The therapeutic actions of Algarve sandwort are attributed to its ability to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, which can help in reducing inflammation and promoting wound healing. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include flavonoids, terpenoids, and alkaloids, which have been identified in various studies as key compounds for the plant's therapeutic properties.
